newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates ease, Buba may drain funds.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates ease, Buba may drain funds.

text.p: German call money rates drifter lower to 2.95/3.00 percent on Tuesday amid ample liquidity conditions which prompted traders to forecast the Bundesbank will likely drain funds from the system this week.
"The liquidity situation is very good right now, banks' holdings at the central bank have risen and so rates are trading a bit lower today," said one senior trader.

After beginning the week on Monday with rates of 3.00/3.05 percent, dealers said the so-called Tuesday float, where additional funds are temporarily in the market, has helped ease conditions. The bulk of trades was conducted at three percent.
In light of ample liquidity conditions, traders said the Bundesbank may decide to drain funds at this week's securities repurchase agreement award on Wednesday.
A 68 billion mark repo pact, set at a fixed three percent rate, expires on Wednesday and traders predict the Bundesbank will drain one to three billion marks.
"I could see them reducing the award by at least one billion marks," said another trader.
Apart from speculation about the tender, dealers said there was very little going on at the moment. "There is no other speculation about any other issue," said one trader.
Bank reserves at the Bundesbank totalled 39.1 billion marks on Monday after 38.6 billion marks on Friday while the monthly average was at 40.0 billion marks down from 40.1 billion marks on Sunday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate FIBOR was set at 3.03867 percent on Tuesday compared with 3.05283 percent on Monday.
